questions.q: How long does a team wait today for a copy of production, and who makes it?
questions.why: Copy time is usually the most visible pain and the easiest win.
questions.need: A team gets a safe copy of production in under an hour
questions.how: Offer self-service clones from approved profiles

questions.q: When did you last restore a database to a precise point in time, and how long did it take?
questions.why: Untested point-in-time recovery is the usual hidden gap.
questions.need: Any database can be restored to a precise point in time, in a known time
questions.how: Restore one production database to a minute and time it

questions.q: How many databases are there, and how many does nobody own clearly?
questions.why: Databases outside any list are the ones that miss backups and patches.
questions.need: Every database is known and has an owner
questions.how: Register databases with the platform and assign owners

questions.q: Which versions are you running, and how far are they from the supported ones?
questions.why: Version spread is effort and risk; it sizes the patching work.
questions.how: Agree target versions and a patch window for the fleet

questions.q: Which production databases have no point-in-time backup today?
questions.why: The answer is the first list of the plan.
questions.need: Every production database has point-in-time backup
questions.how: Apply a backup policy to the databases without one

questions.q: How are test copies masked, if at all?
questions.why: Unmasked copies of production are a common data leak.
questions.need: Test copies are masked before a team sees them
questions.how: Mask sensitive columns as part of cloning

questions.q: Which databases must survive a server failure without anyone acting?
questions.why: Separates what needs a cluster from what does not.
questions.need: Databases that must survive a server failure do so with nobody acting
questions.how: Cluster the ones that need it, and test a failure

questions.q: Who is woken up when a backup fails, and how quickly do they know?
questions.why: A failed backup nobody sees is no backup.
questions.need: A failed backup wakes the right person within minutes
questions.how: Route backup alerts to a named on-call owner
